source: NAR Pending Home Sales Index, Oct. 2026; HousingWire

headline: Contract signings
hit a *record low*
slides.fig_caption: NAR Pending Home Sales Index, Oct. 2026 (2001 average = 100)
slides.sub: The second straight record low: down 4.7% from September and 16.7% from a year ago.

slides.title: Pending sales vs. a year ago, *by region*
slides.note: All four regions also fell from September. *The West dropped most (6.9%)*, while the Midwest dipped 2.7%.

slides.label: Chicago's yearly drop, among the *10 smallest* of big U.S. metros
slides.body: Chicago-Naperville-Elgin ranked fifth for the smallest decline among the 50 largest metros, per Realtor.com Economics. Contracts fell year over year in all 50.

slides.title: The bottom *may be here*
slides.body: NAR's Lawrence Yun says October could mark this cycle's low for contracts, since rates appear to have peaked. Expect thin closings through year-end, and stay close to buyers who paused. They may move fast if rates ease.
